steps.text: Place the ground beef and chopped onion in a skillet over medium heat; cook and stir until the beef is completely browned and the onions are translucent. Drain the fat from the skillet and return it to medium heat. Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, and vinegar. Reduce heat to medium low and simmer 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Hodie’s Sloppy Joes
raw_recipe.description: Ground beef and onions are simmered with tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar to make this vintage Sloppy Joes recipe.
raw_recipe.name: Hodie’s Sloppy Joes

recipeInstructions.text: Place the ground beef and chopped onion in a skillet over medium heat; cook and stir until the beef is completely browned and the onions are translucent. Drain the fat from the skillet and return it to medium heat. Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, and vinegar. Reduce heat to medium low and simmer 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I basically followed the recipe and it was pretty good, just a tad too sweet. I also threw in a clove of garlic with the onion, some red pepper flakes, and a splash of worsheshire sauce
Turned out great! I made this for a potluck at work. All I added to the recipe was diced onions and green pepper and cooked it in a slow cooker. Needless to say, there was no leftovers.
Put in 2 8-oz cans Roasted Garlic tomato sauce, no ketchup, reduced brown sugar by half, added garlic powder and 2 t Worcestershire sauce. Simmered 20 mins.
This is my go to Sloppy Joe recipe. I found it a Tab to sweet as well so I cut the brown sugar to 1 TBS, added 1/2 tsp of garlic powder and 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce.

Exactly the recipe I wanted. Ketchup already is too sweet in my opinion so I leave out the brown sugar and put in a small amount of molasses instead. I have some (unseasoned) rice vinegar in the ketchup as well because I just like that tang it gives and rice vinegar does not have the strong flavor apple cider vinegar does. So happy to find one of the rare sloppy joe recipes that aren't just boiling ground beef in cola sweet ketchup!

This was good, however, I did make some changes based on other people's reviews. I added fresh garlic and omitted the onion because my son will not eat anything with onions in it. I added some onion powder, fresh ground pepper, a pinch of red pepper flakes and some Worcestershire sauce. I topped the sandwiches off with French Fried Onions (for those in the family that like onions). Turned out delicious this way.

I added garlic to the beef and onion mixture and a splash of worchestershire sauce while everything was simmering as I don't like really sweet sloppy Joes. The worchestershire sauce helped cut the sweetness and added a nice flavour.

Excellent recipe. Definitely take the full 20 minutes for it to simmer. Also I added some finely chopped green pepper and a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Next time I might try Sriracha Ketchup instead of plain.

My anti-Sloppy Joe daughter ate half her sandwich and said this was better than what I usually fix (with a store-bought powdered mix). My husband had three sandwiches and finished my daughter's other half. He said they were the best he's ever had! ~~When browning the meat & onions I added some garlic powder and ground in some black pepper. Continued according to the recipe. Tasted and decided it needed something more. I added Worcestershire sauce and ground mustard (not prepared). Tasted & added a little more. This will likely be our go-to Sloppy Joes recipe!

Added some red pepper flakes, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder and worcestershire sauce to experiment as in other recipes. I also added chopped carrots and mushrooms because I wanted to use up extra veggies in the fridge. Very good! Easy.
Came Out Amazing, My Family Loved Them! Only Difference Was That I Added 1 Tablespoon Of Dark Chili Powder, and Yummy! Never Will I Buy Canned Sloppy Joes Again! ;)
Super simple and almost always have the ingredients on hand.
This has become my "go to" sloppy joe recipe. Easy and good!

I'd say these are pretty good but instead of regular brown sugar I used Swerve brown sugar that's an alternative to regular sugar since I'm trying to cut back on sugar & instead of regular ketchup I used sugar free those who said it was too sweet could use an alternative brown sugar like Swerve or use one tablespoon of brown sugar instead of 2 or leave it out completely also this is the first time I've ever used ACV in a recipe so it was different but gave it a little flavor too I don't think it was overpowering at all but if someone didn't like it then they could leave it out but what I loved most about this recipe was that it had very few ingredients unlike some where they have a ton & sometimes less is better & not overpowering especially when it comes to a simple one like Sloppy Joes you don't want to overdo it!!!!!
Love this receipe. I will use this receipe from now on No more canned sloppy joe mix its such a easy dinner to make for my family.
Love it! This will be my go to sloppy Joe recipe! No more canned Manwhich for me.
Loved it! I like it so much that I've 3 times in the last 2 weeks
I will never use can mix again! Delicious! Has. Mild sweetness to it but not overly sweet. I just added some pepper. Next time I might add green peppers.
